Published discharge: the parts a manifest lists

Source: R/wet_catalog.R
wet_catalog.Rd

Reads the manifest.json of a published discharge tree and returns one row per parquet part, with where to fetch it and how to check it. The tree is s3://fresh-bc/discharge/fwa/v1/, read anonymously over HTTPS. The bucket allows no listing, so the manifest is how a reader finds the keys.

Usage

wet_catalog(manifest = getOption("wet.catalog_url", wet_catalog_url))

Arguments

manifest

Path or URL of a manifest.json. The default is option wet.catalog_url, or else the published discharge manifest.

Value

data.frame(dataset, scenario, forcing, source, code, drainage, key, href, rows, bytes, md5), one row per part. key is the part's path below the manifest, and href is where to fetch it. Attributes: manifest (where it was read from), id (e.g. discharge/fwa/v1), built (UTC), provenance (a named list: wet version and commit, and the code that built and published it), sources (a data frame describing each source, with its citation), and source_provenance (a list by source: what each source's rows were built from, e.g. the routed table's fingerprint or the balance's fit release).

Layout

A dataset ID is <variable>/<network>/<version>/<unit>_<timebase>, e.g. discharge/fwa/v1/segment_monthly. The same ID is the S3 prefix, the crate schema key (crate::crt_schema_conform(df, "nge", <ID>)), and, with the variable as the schema and the rest joined by _, the Postgres table wet_db_load() writes (discharge.fwa_v1_segment_monthly). Under each dataset, parts sit at scenario=<s>/forcing=<f>/source=<src>/part-<code>.parquet:

scenario

The emissions pathway: historical, later ssp245 and ssp585.

forcing

The climate data that drove the estimate: PNWNAmet (PCIC's historical run), a GCM as PCIC spells it, climr (the open water balance's 1981-2010 normals), or ensemble.

source

Who made the estimate and how, <group>_<method>: pcic_routed (PCIC's routed flow placed on the FWA) or wet_balance (wet's open water balance).

code

What the part holds. A monthly dataset's part holds one FWA top-level drainage, the first field of fwa_watershed_code (100 for the Fraser); a daily dataset's holds one watershed group (BULK). drainage names it.

The three keys are in the path, not in the files: duckdb's read_parquet(<hrefs>, hive_partitioning = true) reads them back from the hrefs. Files are overwritten in place when the data are rebuilt, so md5 identifies a build, and a read during a publish can find a part that no longer matches its manifest entry: retry once the publish completes. Each publish rewrites the whole manifest from one local tree.

See also

wet_db_load() to load one scenario of a dataset into Postgres.

Examples

# the manifest of a tiny made-up tree, laid out as the published one
cat <- wet_catalog(system.file("extdata", "discharge_manifest.json",
                               package = "wet"))
cat[c("dataset", "scenario", "forcing", "source", "code", "rows")]
#>                              dataset   scenario  forcing      source code rows
#> 1     discharge/fwa/v1/segment_daily historical    climr wet_balance SALR  730
#> 2     discharge/fwa/v1/segment_daily historical PNWNAmet pcic_routed SALR  730
#> 3   discharge/fwa/v1/segment_monthly historical    climr wet_balance  100   26
#> 4   discharge/fwa/v1/segment_monthly historical PNWNAmet pcic_routed  100   26
#> 5 discharge/fwa/v1/watershed_monthly historical    climr wet_balance  100   13
attr(cat, "sources")[c("source", "description")]
#>        source             description
#> 1 pcic_routed  Made-up routed values.
#> 2 wet_balance Made-up balance values.
